You are comparing calendar events to detect duplicates.

**New Event:**
- Title: Quarterly Planning
- Start: 2026-09-11T17:00:00
- End: 2026-09-11T18:00:00
- Location: Video call
- Description: Rescheduled from the 4th. Same agenda.

**Existing Events (same date):**

1. Event ID: event-001
   - Title: Quarterly Planning
   - Start: 2026-09-04T17:00:00
   - End: 2026-09-04T18:00:00
   - Location: Video call
   - Description: Quarterly planning session.

2. Event ID: event-002
   - Title: Quarterly Budget Review
   - Start: 2026-09-11T19:00:00
   - End: 2026-09-11T20:00:00
   - Location: Video call
   - Description: Finance review, separate meeting.

**Question:** Is the new event the same as any of the existing events?

Consider events the same if they refer to the same real-world event, even if:
- Wording is slightly different
- One has more details than the other
- Time changed slightly (updates)

Return the matching Event ID (or null if no match) and brief reasoning.

trace.raw_response_text: {"matched_event_id": "event-001", "reasoning": "The new event is titled 'Quarterly Planning' with the same time (17:00-18:00) and location (Video call) as event-001. Its description says it was rescheduled from the 4th with the same agenda, which identifies it as the same meeting moved to a new date. Event-002 is a different meeting ('Quarterly Budget Review') at a different time, with a description marking it as separate."}

description: S5: a plain-text email moves an event to a new date. The existing event is on the old date, so it is outside the new date's candidate window -- only a thread hint can reach it. Included so the LLM rung does not merge it wrongly if identity ever falls through.
